notes: City with governmental funds on modified cash basis and utility (enterprise) funds on accrual basis; basis recorded as cash for the governmental roll-forward. Governmental receipts/disbursements are the Total Governmental Funds column of the Statement of Revenues, Expenditures and Changes in Fund Balances (p5); bond proceeds 566,667 are printed inside Total revenues (reported_totals includes debt_proceeds) and recorded in debt_proceeds, not receipts. Transfer from (to) other funds (1,056,846) is the total column net; recorded as transfers_out (General Fund out 1,648,252 = Street in 529,331 + Joint Fire in 62,075 + net to enterprise funds 1,056,846; Dump Fund returned 1,816). Beginning cash 2,662,874 and ending 2,062,059 are total governmental fund balances (all cash, CDs and county treasurer cash). Balance sheet is the government-wide Statement of Net Position Total column (p1), which mixes modified cash (governmental) and accrual (business-type); component unit (Wisner Care Center) excluded. Business-type from Statement of Revenues, Expenses and Changes in Net Position - Proprietary Funds Total column (p7): receipts = operating revenues 3,256,571 + nonoperating interest, city sales tax and grant income; disbursements = operating expenses 3,542,324 + interest expense, loan fees, bond issuance costs; beginning net position 7,630,678 as originally reported plus restatement 705,409 (restated 8,336,087); 7,630,678 + 1,395,949 + 1,056,846 + 705,409 = 10,788,882. Proprietary cash flow Total column on p9. Detail: General Fund departmental combining statement (p14-15) is more detailed than the General Fund budgetary comparison schedule (p10), so only the departmental schedule is recorded for the General Fund (no budget amounts; budget on p10 not recorded to avoid double counting); Street, Dinklage Foundation and Joint Fire budgetary schedules recorded with budget_final. Detail expenditure categories: function by department, but capital outlay, economic development and debt lines use their own category so the function split ties to the statement (general government 190,187, public safety 320,624, public works 3,298 = cemetery excl. debt, culture/recreation 226,905, capital outlay 675,747). Cemetery operating costs follow the statement's Public works (streets/highways). Enterprise fund-by-fund detail not recorded (only the proprietary statement with fund columns exists). Zero-actual lines not recorded. Transfer cross-check: Street 529,331 and Joint Fire 62,075 transfers in agree with the General Fund transfers out; the Water and Sewer fund transfers in (529,331 each) agree with the proprietary statement. Read pages 1-15 of 15
